MiMedx Group, FY ending 2012-12-31. Management says: Financing cash flow decrease due to lower warrant/option exercises and Surgical Biologics acquisition payment (E30)
Numbers show: Describes financing cash flow components; does not address operating cash flow or receivables per E30
Fit in sample 1: fits. Evidence: E30.
Questions for management: What drove the 248.6% revenue growth (organic demand, acquisitions, channel loading, pricing)? Why did receivables grow 304.5% vs 248.6% revenue growth, pushing DSO from 89 to 103 days? What specific changes in credit terms, customer mix, or shipment timing explain the receivables buildup? Why did operating cash flow improve less than net income (CFO -$3.4M vs NI -$7.7M in 2012)? Were there changes in payment terms, channel stuffing, or revenue recognition timing that contributed to the revenue and receivables patterns? What were the primary drivers of the 248.6% revenue increase (e.g., volume, price, new products, acquisitions, channel loading)? Why did receivables grow 304.5% versus 248.6% revenue growth, and why did DSO increase from 89 to 103 days (e.g., longer payment terms, shipment timing, customer mix)? What specific working-capital or non-cash items drove the $3.3M improvement in operating cash flow despite continued net losses and a large receivables build? What specific demand drivers (new products, market expansion, pricing, acquisitions) caused the 248.6% revenue increase? Why did receivables grow 304.5% vs 248.6% revenue growth, pushing DSO from 89 to 103 days — was this due to longer payment terms, channel loading, shipment timing, or collection issues? What portion of the revenue growth came from the Surgical Biologics acquisition (referenced in E30 as a $427K financing outflow), and what was the acquired revenue contribution? Why did operating cash flow remain negative (-$3.4M) despite $19.3M incremental revenue? What working capital changes (receivables, inventory, payables) drove the gap? Can you provide quarterly revenue and receivables data to assess whether Q4 shipment timing or channel loading inflated year-end receivables?

Columbia Sportswear, FY ending 2015-12-31. Management says: No explanation for 2015 receivables or operating cash flow movements is present in the provided MD&A excerpts. The only cash flow discussion (E47) covers 2014 vs 2013.
Numbers show: Receivables grew 8% ($344.4M → $372.0M) while revenue grew 10.7%; DSO improved 60→58 days annually (E7, E18, E23). But quarterly signals show Q3 receivables +15.5% vs revenue +13.7% (DSO 62→63) and Q4 receivables +8.0% vs revenue +3.3% (DSO 46→48), indicating late-year shipment timing (E27, E28). Operating cash flow fell 49% ($185.8M → $95.1M) while net income rose 27% ($137.2M → $174.3M) (E5, E6, E16, E17, E24).
Fit in sample 3: unverified. Evidence: E5, E6, E7, E16, E17, E18, E23, E24, E27, E28, E47.
Questions for management: What specific working capital components (inventory, accounts payable, accrued liabilities, taxes) drove the $90.7M year-over-year decline in operating cash flow? Did payment terms to wholesale customers or international distributors change in 2015, contributing to the H2 receivables buildup? Was there intentional channel loading (earlier or larger fall shipments) in Q3/Q4 that pulled forward revenue? How much of the 2015 inventory increase (if any) was strategic build for 2016 vs. slow-moving stock? What specific working capital changes (inventory, accounts payable, accrued liabilities, tax payments) drove the $90.7M year-over-year decline in operating cash flow despite higher net income? Did the May 2015 ERP implementation in international distributor businesses cause temporary billing or collection disruptions that reduced cash collections in H2 2015? How much of the Q3 receivables surge (+15.5%) reflects normal fall-season shipment timing versus channel loading or extended terms to distributors? What is the expected cash flow impact of the Japan ERP transition planned for 2016? What specific working capital changes (inventory, receivables, payables, accruals) drove the $90.7M decline in operating cash flow despite a $37.1M increase in net income? Does the Q3/Q4 receivables surge (outpacing revenue) reflect pull-forward of fall shipments, extended terms to wholesale customers, or ERP transition issues in international distributor businesses (mentioned in E30)? How much of the 2015 revenue growth is organic vs. the prAna acquisition timing effect (incremental 5 months), and what is the expected run-rate contribution going forward?
